samples.summary: Symlink containment covers only the lenses directory itself, not the files inside it — a symlinked `<id>.md` or `lenses.json` is read through and its bytes end up in the model prompt and in the snapshot pushed to the public eval store
samples.evidence: The guard resolves and re-checks only the directory: `const real = realpathSync(dir); if (!insideTree(realpathSync(repoRoot), real))` (replay-plan.mjs:261-264). Everything below it — `readFileSync(path.join(real, "lenses.json"))` (line 275) and, inside `buildConfig`, `readFileSync(path.join(lensesDir, `${l.id}.md`))` (config-build.mjs:171) — uses ordinary `readFileSync`, which follows symlinks. Nothing in scripts/ ever calls `lstatSync`/`isSymbolicLink` (grep for `lstatSync|isSymbolicLink|O_NOFOLLOW` in scripts/: no matches), so the file-level link is never seen. Vector: commit a branch containing `scripts/agent/lenses-x/lenses.json` (a real file declaring one lens `security`) plus `scripts/agent/lenses-x/security.md -> /proc/self/environ` (or any absolute path on the runner), dispatch eval-replay with `lenses_dir: scripts/agent/lenses-x` and `panel: real`. The directory is in-tree, so every check in `planLensConfig` passes and the preflight prints a config_hash. The paid leg then runs `run.mjs`, whose `buildConfig(opts.lensesDir, …)` (run.mjs:863) reads that symlink from inside a process whose environment holds `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_1..8` (eval-replay.yml:379-393). The bytes become `rubric_text` in the snapshot, are handed to the model as the lens rubric (`materializeLenses` → `--lenses-dir matLenses`, run.mjs:926/1151), are stored as `configSnapshot` in the run (run.mjs:914/1258), uploaded as an artifact, and pushed by the `collect` job into the PUBLIC store `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` (eval-replay.yml:540) — permanent git history. The docblock at replay-plan.mjs:214-216 explicitly claims the symlink case is covered ("the check is made again after `realpath`, because a committed symlink is a lexically innocent path"), so the gate reads as complete while covering only one of the two link positions. Precondition is repo write access (workflow_dispatch), which is why confidence is medium rather than high; impact if reached is credential disclosure into a public repository.

samples.summary: Containment is "inside the workspace directory", not "committed to this repository" — `.eval-store/` (a clone of a different repo made earlier in the same job) and `node_modules/` are inside REPO_ROOT and are accepted as a lens configuration
samples.evidence: `REPO_ROOT` is derived from the module's location (replay-plan.mjs:57) and `insideTree(repoRoot, dir)` (line 246) only asks whether the resolved path is under that directory. But both jobs run `git clone … .eval-store` into that same directory (eval-replay.yml:164 and :248) and the replay job runs `npm ci` into `scripts/agent/node_modules` (eval-replay.yml:256). So `lenses_dir: .eval-store/anything` or `lenses_dir: scripts/agent/node_modules/<pkg>/lenses` passes containment, passes the `lenses.json` and `buildConfig` checks, and the resulting rubric text becomes the panel's instructions to a model holding the Claude credential — while the error message the guard prints for the rejecting case asserts the opposite invariant ("it has to be something this repository committed", line 249). The eval store is a separate repository whose contents are not reviewed by this repo's gates. A provenance check (e.g. `git ls-files --error-unmatch` on the resolved dir, or restricting the input to a fixed prefix such as `scripts/agent/lenses*`) is what the stated invariant needs; a location check is not it.

samples.summary: The preflight validates a TRIMMED copy of `lenses_dir` while the runner is handed the raw value — the path proved free is not necessarily the path opened
samples.evidence: `planLensConfig` normalises with `const asked = typeof value === "string" ? value.trim() : ""` (replay-plan.mjs:231) and resolves/validates that trimmed string. The workflow, by contrast, forwards the raw environment value: `if [ -n "$LENSES_DIR" ]; then ARGS+=(--lenses-dir "$LENSES_DIR")` (eval-replay.yml:420-421), and `run.mjs` resolves it verbatim with `path.resolve(args["lenses-dir"] …)` (run.mjs:796) with no validation of its own. On a POSIX runner `"lenses "` and `"lenses"` are different names, so a dispatch value with leading/trailing whitespace makes the preflight validate, hash and print one directory while the paid leg reads another. Most divergences fail closed (the untrimmed name does not exist), but the validated-value/used-value mismatch is the pattern that makes a guard unsound; either trim in the workflow too, or validate the raw string.

samples.summary: The lenses-dir containment guard lives only in the preflight process; the code that actually opens the directory (`run.mjs` → `buildConfig`) accepts any path, including absolute ones and `../` climbs
samples.evidence: `resolveRunOptions` does `lensesDir: path.resolve(args["lenses-dir"] ?? path.join(HERE, "..", "lenses"))` (run.mjs:796) with no containment, no existence and no provenance check, and `buildConfig` (config-build.mjs:160-186) reads whatever it is given. The only thing standing between the dispatch input and that read is `replay-plan.mjs` being invoked earlier, in a different process, by the workflow (eval-replay.yml:196 and :280). That holds today, but the guard is not on the enforced path: reordering or removing the "Resolve which pull refs this corpus needs" step, or any future caller of `run.mjs`/`review-panel.mjs --lenses-dir`, reaches the read unguarded while the preflight's docblock reads as though the value is proved. Searched: grep for `lenses-dir|lensesDir|LENSES_DIR` across the repo (call sites: eval-replay.yml, agent-review-panel.yml:886, agent-review-on-demand.yml:391, spec-to-pr.mjs:315, cache-report.mjs:248, review-panel.mjs:2485, run.mjs:796, config-build.mjs:270) — none of them validates containment; grep for `insideTree|realpathSync` outside replay-plan.mjs — no other containment implementation exists.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. planLensConfig realpaths and re-checks containment only for the directory node (replay-plan.mjs:261-264); every file beneath it is opened with plain symlink-following reads — readFileSync(path.join(real,"lenses.json")) at replay-plan.mjs:266/275 and readFileSync(path.join(lensesDir, `${id}.md`)) at config-build.mjs:170-171. assertSafeLensId (config-build.mjs:88-98) only sanitizes the id string, not the resolved target. Grep confirms no lstatSync/isSymbolicLink/O_NOFOLLOW anywhere in scripts/, and the only symlink test (replay-plan.test.mjs:724-737) exercises the directory case only, so the file-level link position is entirely uncovered while the docblock at replay-plan.mjs:211-216 asserts the symlink case is handled. The sink chain is real: run.mjs:796 resolves --lenses-dir with no containment check at all, run.mjs:863 buildConfig yields a snapshot inlining rubric_text (config-build.mjs:208), stored as configSnapshot (run.mjs:914,1258) and materialized for the model (run.mjs:926,1151), inside a job whose env holds CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and _1.._8 (eval-replay.yml:379-394), with the collect job pushing to dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval (eval-replay.yml:469,540). lenses_dir is an operator-supplied workflow_dispatch input (eval-replay.yml:113,399,421). Path traversal / sensitive-data exposure is in the security lane; the write-access precondition narrows the attacker set but does not make the path unreachable, so no not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.
